name: Ruinborn
kit: A pry-bar, a hooded lamp, 30ft of knotted line, and a map of one dead city drawn in your own hand.
text: You were born in the bones of a city that died before your grandparents. You know which floors hold and which drop, which stairwells flood, and how to be somewhere else by the time anyone comes looking.

name: Waystation
kit: A ledger of debts and favours, a good coat, and a mule that tolerates you.
text: You grew up where the roads cross, watching every kind of traveller come through and learning which ones paid. You can read a stranger's boots and know how far they have walked and whether they can afford dinner.

name: Deepholt
kit: A sealed shelter-suit patch kit, a hand-crank lantern, and a key to a door that no longer exists.
text: Your people went underground when the Silence came and did not come up for three generations. You were raised on rationing, sealed doors, and the old machines that kept the air moving — and on the certainty that the surface is a place you visit, not a place you trust.

name: Nomad Convoy
kit: A weatherproof bedroll, a driving whip, and a share in a wagon you may never see again.
text: Home was a column of wagons that never stopped for long. You can sleep through anything, drive a team through worse, and you learned early that a place you cannot leave is a trap.

name: The Reach
kit: A working tool that doubles as a weapon, a season of preserved food, and a grudge against something in the hills.
text: A holdfast at the frontier, too far out for help to arrive and too stubborn to move. Everyone worked, everyone stood watch, and the difference between a farmer and a soldier was which one the night demanded.

name: Cloister
kit: A copied book you were not supposed to take, ink, and a letter of introduction to someone who may be dead.
text: An order that spent the Silence copying what it could before it rotted. You can read three scripts nobody speaks any more, and you were taught that knowing a thing and being permitted to use it are different questions.

name: Scavenger
text: You went into places people do not come out of, and you came out. Repeatedly. The work is patience, a good light, and knowing the exact moment to stop being greedy.

name: Warden
text: You stood a wall, escorted a caravan, or held a gate. Nothing glorious — a wage, a spear, and the understanding that most of the job is being visibly unafraid at the right moment.

name: Mender
text: You learned medicine the way it is learned now: on people who were already dying, with what was in the bag. You have a steady hand and a very short list of things that still frighten you.

name: Tinker
text: Salvage in, something that works out. You repair what the old world left, and when it cannot be repaired you make it into three things that can.

name: Broker
text: You moved goods, information, and occasionally people, between parties who would rather not meet. Everyone you have ever dealt with thinks they got the better end.

name: Acolyte
text: You were apprenticed to someone who could do the impossible and was unbearable about it. You swept their floor for years and learned the shape of the work by watching.

name: Hunter
text: You fed people by knowing where things go to drink and how long to wait. The Silence left animals that hunt back, so you also learned when to leave.

name: Outrider
text: You rode ahead of the column and came back with the truth about what was in front of it. Fast, alone, and paid to be right.

name: The Collapse
text: Something came down — a structure, a settlement, an expedition — and you were the one who walked out. You have never entirely decided whether that was luck or a debt, and nobody who could tell you is still alive.

name: Cast Out
text: You were named for something, fairly or otherwise, and told not to come back. You travel light and you have a very clear sense of which doors are closed to you.

name: The Debt
text: Someone spent something they could not spare to keep you alive, and they are still owed. It is not a metaphor and they have not forgotten.

name: The Vision
text: Something reached you once — in fever, in a ruin, in the quiet after — and told you a true thing you had no way of knowing. You have been trying to work out what it wanted ever since.

name: The Bargain
text: You traded something of yourself for something you needed more, and the exchange held. You do not talk about the terms, and you check them, quietly, more often than you admit.

name: Left for Dead
text: People you trusted made a decision about you and walked away. You survived it, which was not the plan, and you have a slow and patient interest in where they went.
